usual_baseline: Pre-operative prophylaxis is nearly always given (85–100%). The problem is after the operation. 77.6–90.2% of uncomplicated cases still get post-operative antibiotics, and courses in complicated cases run long (mean 7.8–9.2 days). Correct agent or dose is often wrong: 2.2% trust-adherent agents in non-allergic patients [2363].
fix_that_works: A written post-operative antibiotic guideline: antibiotics withheld in uncomplicated cases rose from 54.3% to 78.3%, and stay fell from 23.3 to 14.5 hours [2851]. Posters, local guideline and an operation note proforma: omission in simple appendicitis 79% to 97%, correct 3–5 day course 12.1% to 61% [2770]. Teaching with the gentamicin calculator: 68.8% to 93.8% [2060].
fix_that_fails: Presenting results at forum and governance plus a theatre poster: uncomplicated cases on antibiotics only fell from 90.2% to 84.4% [2767]. Consultant teaching and an electronic theatre note: duration in complicated cases only 9.2 to 8.4 days [2868]. Course length in complicated appendicitis stayed inconsistent, 20% in a later cycle [2770].
consultant_advice: Pre-operative prophylaxis is not worth auditing again; it is almost always given. Audit post-operative antibiotics in uncomplicated appendicitis and course length in complicated cases. Pair it with a written stopping rule in the operation note, and measure length of stay, which one audit showed can fall by 9 hours.
